rationale: PCR prevalence survey in sled dogs; three dogs were 'undergoing treatment' but no signs, therapy or outcome are described.

species: Babesia sp. (North Carolina large piroplasm, PCR)
rationale: One immunosuppressed lymphoma dog with incidental parasitaemia treated with imidocarb twice; PCR stayed positive to 50 weeks (treatment failure). Clinical syndrome is weak but treatment failure cases are eligible.
Diagnostic PCR paper; therapy monitoring is mentioned (atovaquone and tilmicosin cleared B. gibsoni, doxycycline and berenil did not) but no clinical presentation of the treated dogs is given.
Narrative review covering epidemiology, diagnosis, treatment and control of canine babesiosis.
Intravenous pharmacokinetics of diminazene in six healthy dogs.
In vitro culture study of ionophores on canine erythrocytes; no infected dogs.
No abstract; title indicates a single co-infection case report that may include treatment and outcome. Needs full text.
Clinic note says etiological and symptomatic treatment gave good effect, but the abstract gives no clinical signs, drugs or numbers. Could be a case series if the full text details them.
No abstract; title suggests an imidocarb treatment evaluation in canine babesiosis, so presentation and outcome are unknown.
In vitro development of a diminazene-resistant strain; no dogs.
One dog with signs of babesiosis; the abstract does not mention treatment or outcome, although the earlier screen noted imidocarb. Needs full text.
Retrospective comparison of doxycycline-enrofloxacin-metronidazole with or without diminazene in naturally infected dogs; efficacy 85.7% vs 83.3% and recovery time reported.

species: Babesia spp. and other CVBD agents
rationale: Field prevention trial of imidacloprid and permethrin with infection incidence as the endpoint.

species: B. gibsoni, B. bovis (in vitro), B. microti (mice)
rationale: In vitro and mouse study of artesunate; no infected dogs.
Case report of anorexia, haemoglobinuria and fever focused on species identification; no treatment or outcome in the abstract.
Hsp70 transcript levels in diminazene-resistant cultured parasites; no dogs.
Labrador bitch with jaundice and hyperbilirubinaemia treated; parasites cleared by day 5 and the dog recovered by day 15.

No abstract; the earlier full-text screen records a German Shepherd with severe anaemia treated with diminazene, oxytetracycline and transfusion. Recorded as uncertain only because the abstract is missing; outcome was not confirmed here.
Labrador bitch with jaundice and hyperbilirubinaemia given antibabesial and supportive therapy; negative by day 5 and fully recovered by day 15 (likely the same case as the other jaundice record).
Tibetan Mastiff puppy with paralysis, low haemoglobin and B. gibsoni on smear, cured after ivermectin and Xuechongjing within 3 days.
Molecular first report in three dogs; no clinical signs, treatment or outcome described.
In vitro nystatin study on cultured parasites and canine cells; no infected dogs.
Acaricide transmission-blocking trial; endpoint is prevention of infection, with no treatment of clinical disease.
Imported puppy with fever, anaemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia and azotaemia; responded to imidocarb and PCR was negative 2 weeks later.
In vitro atovaquone-resistant strain with cytb SNP; no dogs.
Vaccine safety study in uninfected dogs.
Puppy with severe anaemia and haemoglobinuria was euthanised; the paper is about post-mortem parasite morphology and describes no treatment.

Twelve naturally infected dogs, partly randomised placebo-controlled; atovaquone plus azithromycin cleared B. conradae DNA on PCR whereas placebo dogs stayed positive. Presentation is thin (haemolytic anaemia only).
A. platys first-detection case with B. vogeli co-infection; laboratory abnormalities only, no treatment or outcome.
Forum recommendations on managing canine vector-borne diseases in general; the abstract does not show whether babesiosis treatment is covered in any detail.
Case report of concurrent Neospora, Babesia and Ehrlichia infection centred on diagnosis; the abstract describes no treatment or outcome.
Dogs treated for tick paralysis by R. sanguineus; Babesia was found in only two and was not the treated condition.
Mitochondrial genes of a diminazene-resistant cultured isolate; no dogs.
Parasite cytb genotyping survey for atovaquone-resistance mutations; no treated dogs described.
Safety study of a candidate vaccine in uninfected dogs.
In vitro energy metabolism of a diminazene-resistant isolate; no dogs.
Duplicate of DOI:10.3906/vet-1201-45; title indicates a molecular first-detection report, with no treatment suggested.
First molecular detection in two dogs; one had pyrexia, weakness and pallor, but no treatment or outcome is described.
Sled dogs with babesiosis (one with TBE co-infection) were 'diagnosed and treated accordingly', but the abstract names no drugs and reports no outcome. Needs full text.
Lymphocyte subsets after vaccination with a soluble parasite antigen in uninfected dogs.
